File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: 11498-11522
Problem: The jq expressions used for candidate-run selection and attribution-log generation independently duplicate the date parsing and tracking-marker capture regex.
Why it fails at runtime: If the regex for capturing the tracking marker or the date parsing logic needs to be updated, having duplicated logic risks the two filters diverging. This would result in the attribution log line (VALIDATION_RUN_ATTRIBUTION) reporting candidate, eligible, or skipped counts that disagree with the actual selection logic applied by the poller, misleading operators during diagnosis.

=== FINDINGS FROM minimax_minimax-m3 ===
File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: line 11497 (`local attribution_tracking="${TRACKING_NUM:-}"`) combined with the jq `select` at lines 11505-11508
Problem: When TRACKING_NUM is unset, the eligibility predicate `(._tracking != "" and $tracking != "" and ._tracking == $tracking) or (._tracking == "" and (.conclusion // "") != "success")` collapses to the second clause only, so every marked run is silently rejected (the first clause fails because `$tracking == ""`). The function would then only return unmarked non-success runs, masking any attribution work.
Why it fails at runtime: Today the sole call site sets TRACKING_NUM, so this is dormant. A future caller that forgets to set the env var would lose attribution for every marked run with no error indication. The comment block above the jq documents the marker-based design but not this precondition.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 2

File: scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh
Line or code reference: lines 11498-11522 (the two jq invocations in get_last_validation_run_info)
Problem: The selection jq encodes the eligibility predicate `(._tracking != "" and $tracking != "" and ._tracking == $tracking) or (._tracking == "" and (.conclusion // "") != "success")`, while the separate attribution jq encodes the inverse classification `if $n != "" and $n != $tracking then "foreign" elif $n == "" and (.conclusion // "") == "success" then "unmarked_success" else "eligible" end`. The two expressions must stay logically inverse; today they are, but the dual encoding invites drift.
Why it fails at runtime: A future tightening or loosening of one filter (for example adding a confidence gate or new conclusion variant) without the matching update to the other would produce VALIDATION_RUN_ATTRIBUTION counts that disagree with the run actually selected, misleading operators diagnosing attribution decisions. The two jq processes also each rescan and reparse the runs JSON.
SEVERITY: NIT
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 3

Requirement: PR description states `get_last_validation_run_info` "logs a `VALIDATION_RUN_ATTRIBUTION` line to stderr"; the README diff and the changelog fragment both advertise it as a new log line. `agents.md` declares the "Stable log prefixes (contractual)" section as the registry where "Renames are breaking unless an alongside-old shim is documented and shipped", and the prefix is pinned by the new tests (test_validation_run_fallback_ignores_success_marked_for_another_tracking_issue and test_validation_run_fallback_ignores_unmarked_success assert on its exact string).
Expected change site: agents.md "Stable log prefixes (contractual)" section — both the prose bulleted list and the parallel `LOG_PREFIX.name=` block (six prior-round reviewers pointed at the same omission, including the same-file confirmation that z-ai/glm-5.2 cited: existing tests/test_orchestrate_poll_workflow_contract.py:128-142 and tests/test_workflow_failure_heal.py:197-201 enforce the "every prefix appears as both `- <prefix>` and `LOG_PREFIX.name=<prefix>`" pattern).
Evidence of absence: No diff hunk in agents.md. VALIDATION_RUN_ATTRIBUTION appears only in scripts/orchestrate_poll_process.sh:11513 (the new stderr echo), README.md:2538 (the bullet describing the new log line), changelog.d/3965-validation-run-attribution.md:11 (the "New log line" table row), and the test assertions. The agents.md prose list and `LOG_PREFIX.name=` block both still end at the previous entry without the new prefix. The AI Materiality Advisory comment posted on this PR (entry 1 of pr_all_comments_context) flagged workflow-YAML changes as high materiality under the deterministic AGENTS.md path rules, which makes the agents.md update doubly expected.
SEVERITY: MAJOR
ISSUE_CONFIDENCE: 5
